summary.text: A 45-year-old man with no previous mental or physical health history, no regular medication and no family history of mental health issues developed pervasive sadness, anhedonia and suicidal thoughts after leaving his job because of workplace bullying, without psychotic symptoms.

Citalopram started by his GP in early March (20 mg, then 40 mg) gave no meaningful mood improvement. In mid-June he attended A&E with severe anxiety and suicidal ideation; he was managed by the Home Treatment Team and started mirtazapine 15 mg nightly.

Two weeks later he ingested household bleach with suicidal intent and was admitted informally to the acute male psychiatric unit in early July. Mirtazapine was increased to 45 mg without improvement, his state deteriorated and he was sectioned under the Mental Health Act for worsening suicidal ideation.

Four weeks after admission citalopram was stopped and fluoxetine 20 mg was added and raised to 40 mg; there was no clinical improvement by mid-September, so the MDT started lamotrigine augmentation at 25 mg once daily with weekly titration for severe treatment-resistant unipolar depression.

Within 3 weeks lamotrigine had reached 50 mg twice daily with significant improvement in mood, engagement and self-care, nearly non-existent suicidal ideation, residual low mood and no adverse effects observed; PHQ-9 fell from 23/27 to 3/27.
